subject: No Cwd.pm shim: `use Cwd` / `require Cwd` both die under PCL, though cwd() is a builtin
description:
DONE s319 (cdb83ae).  lib/Cwd.pm now exists.

cwd/getcwd/fastcwd/fastgetcwd/getdcwd delegate to the cwd() builtin.
abs_path/realpath/fast_abs_path/fast_realpath are implemented IN PERL over
readlink/-l/-e — CLAUDE.md 9a, and every primitive was verified to work before
the shim was written.  They are NOT aliased to cwd(), which this task warned
against: abs_path must resolve symlinks, and a shim silently returning an
unresolved path is worse than a missing module.

SEMANTICS PINNED AGAINST REAL PERL 5.40.3 FIRST — several are not obvious and
would have been got wrong by guessing:
  abs_path("existing/newfile") SUCCEEDS  — only the DIRECTORY part must exist
  abs_path("missing/x")        undef
  an ABSOLUTE symlink target discards everything resolved so far
  abs_path("") and abs_path()  cwd;   abs_path("/") -> "/"
  ".." resolves textually against the already-resolved prefix
  symlink loop -> undef after 32 hops (no hang)

VERIFIED byte-identical to perl across 15 cases.  Gate 124/4461 PASS, sweep
0 new / 0 fixed.  Regression test in Pl/t/transpile-test-08.t builds its own
symlink tree so it does not depend on the checkout layout.

NOT DONE (nobody needed it yet, and guessing would be worse than the gap):
`Cwd::chdir` (the exported chdir override that keeps $ENV{PWD} in sync) is not
provided — real Cwd exports it only on request.  Add it if a module asks.

File::Spec's rel2abs deliberately still calls the cwd() BUILTIN rather than
requiring Cwd — Cwd::cwd() is that same builtin, so the require would only add
a module load to every base-less rel2abs.  The reason is recorded in the file.
